method: Decode the published, possibly re-encoded WebM. Inspect every encoded 25 fps frame of the first 3.48-second gesture in shoulder/elbow/wrist contact sheets; also inspect full-character keyframes and full-video scene samples. No new browser session.

duplicateStats.method: Exact SHA-256 equality of decoded RGB images for the sampled 87 encoded video frames; this measures repeated captured images, not GPU presentation or lost browser draws.
Exact SHA-256 equality of decoded RGB images for the sampled 87 encoded video frames; this measures repeated captured images, not GPU presentation or lost browser draws.

criteria: Shoulder, elbow and wrist remain connected in every reviewed encoded first-gesture frame; no duplicate hand, open sleeve hole or persistent residual arm was visible.
Head, pale-blue hair, clothing and shoes retain the supplied character identity. The hand lifts beside the face, changes wrist pose and returns to the neutral silhouette.
Thirteen full-character poses per profile and eleven full-video scene samples were viewed, including keyboard focus, paused/reduced-motion portions and theme/navigation ending.
Four clean locale/theme screenshots and both before/after contact sheets were viewed. Clean screenshots contain no QA timer overlay.
limitations: Visual review covers every one of 87 encoded frames in the first 3.48-second gesture per profile plus selected full-video scenes; it does not inspect every encoded frame of the entire video.
The recording is nominally 25 fps (40 ms spacing). The decoded QA timer values below are actual selections, not a guarantee of 40 ms precision or input latency.

The browser recorder can repeat captured frames or omit intermediate browser draws. Zero exact decoded RGB repeats does not prove that all GPU-presented frames were captured: the changing background and lossy encoder can alter pixels independently.
Lossy VP8 compression produces occasional brief soft/blocky frames, especially near recovery. Connected anatomy and the final rest pose remain readable; the public video is not lossless.
A visible focus ring during keyboard interaction is the intended accessibility state. The QA timer is a temporary recording overlay, not website UI.
The mobile profile uses desktop Chrome touch/viewport emulation. Keyboard evidence in that profile is an emulated external keyboard, not a physical mobile device.
